name: Laura Pettit

five_sec.what_is_it: A recipe box app with a meal planner and grocery list
five_sec.who_for: Folks who keep their own recipes and like to plan
five_sec.trust_why: It says 'Free Trial - no card required!' in plain words, which I like, and the ratings look real
five_sec.next_step: Look for the price and the word 'cancel'
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It's App Store and Google Play buttons and 'Recipes, Meal Plans and Grocery Lists'

full_page.what_stopped_me: I'd have to find and check every gluten-free recipe myself, which is the exact work I pay eMeals to do. And a countdown to a '50% OFF' sale makes me want to wait and see
full_page.whats_missing: Anything gluten-free or celiac; whether 'Deliver Groceries' works with Walmart

PTE.quote: Bless them for writing 'we don't auto-bill when your year ends.' But it's an empty recipe box, and I'd be reading three labels a night again.

five_sec.what_is_it: Some kind of app that picks dinner for you
five_sec.trust_why: Never heard of it, and the big orange button is a 'Letter from the CEO' instead of telling me what it costs
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Pictures of finished plates on a phone; I can't tell if they send anything

full_page.what_stopped_me: The FAQ says a free 1-month trial and 'prices are available when you download the app', then the pricing page says $25 a month for 'messages'. Two stories. And it says the computer writes the recipe itself; I'm not trusting a machine with soy sauce
full_page.whats_missing: One word about gluten or celiac; a single clear price

OL.quote: One page says a free month, the other says $25 a month for 'messages.' Which is it? And a robot writing Ava's recipes, no ma'am.

five_sec.what_is_it: eMeals, the meal plan app I already use
five_sec.trust_why: It works, but I had that renewal fight with them and I haven't forgotten
five_sec.next_step: Check what it costs this year
five_sec.delivers_food_why: I know it's recipes and a list, not a box

full_page.what_stopped_me: Still no price on the front page, a pop-up to 'Unlock This Special Offer', and right there in the help center: 'Why you might see a pending charge before your billing date.' The Gluten Free plan says 'gluten allergy or sensitivity', not celiac
full_page.whats_missing: Price and renewal date up front; celiac-level wording

EM.quote: Same as ever: 'Gluten Free… allergy or sensitivity,' no price on the front, and a help article about pending charges before billing. I know that one, y'all.

five_sec.what_is_it: It plans dinners, texts the family to vote, and sends the list to a Walmart or Instacart cart
five_sec.trust_why: It says 'no card needed' and 'We don't deliver food' right up front; I'd still want to read the fine print
five_sec.next_step: Find the price and how you cancel
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The green line under the paragraph says they don't deliver food

full_page.what_stopped_me: Billing looks honest: 'Your free Family days need no card, so nothing can be charged.' And the Walmart cart is free, which fits my Walmart+. But gluten-free is a little tag on the sample week and one line, 'Dietary needs (gluten-free…) are respected on every plan'. Nobody says celiac, nobody says they checked broth or soy sauce, and the sample is sized 'serves 4', which won't feed Cole
full_page.whats_missing: A real gluten-free sample week with the ingredients shown; the word celiac; bigger portions for a teenager

DD.quote: 'Your free Family days need no card, so nothing can be charged.' I read that twice. But 'gluten-free' as a little tag — did anybody check the broth?

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal kit boxes, with a pick-a-box prize pop-up
five_sec.trust_why: A game to 'reveal your offer' before it tells me anything
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The boxes and '10 Free Meals' at the bottom

full_page.what_stopped_me: The fine print says 'auto-renewing subscription' and there's no gluten-free plan in that long list of plans. Shared kitchens are a no for celiac
full_page.whats_missing: A gluten-free plan; a price without a zip code

HF.quote: A box to 'reveal your offer' and fine print that says 'auto-renewing subscription.' I've been burned once. And not one gluten-free plan on that list.

dd_offer.why: It says no card in three places and the pricing box says you just go back to the free plan
dd_offer.expect_day_15: It goes back to the free plan, and since they never had my card they can't charge it. I'd still check my bank statement, bless it.

head_to_head.reason: Three years on a real gluten-free plan beats a gluten-free tag I can't check yet; I'd only switch for something clearly safer

EM.reason: eMeals has a whole Gluten Free plan; DinnerDrop's billing is kinder but it hasn't shown me the gluten-free is checked

PTE.reason: Plan to Eat makes me find every gluten-free recipe myself; DinnerDrop at least plans gluten-free and fills my Walmart cart

OL.reason: DinnerDrop tells me plainly what it costs; Ollie tells me two different things

HF.reason: No auto-renewing box and no shared kitchen; it's my own groceries

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: On the home page sample week, make the 'Gluten-free' tab show a full celiac-safe week with ingredients listed, plus one sentence on how gluten-free is checked (soy sauce, broth, seasoning packets) and the reminder to read labels.
